## Android

### AND-001: Cleartext (plain HTTP) traffic is allowed

**Severity:** high · **Profiles:** MAS-L1 · **Confidence:** high · **Effort:** minutes

**Why it matters:** Plain HTTP can be read and changed by anyone on the same network, such as public Wi-Fi. Tokens and personal data sent this way are exposed.

**Fix:** Remove `cleartextTrafficPermitted="true"` from the base config (and `android:usesCleartextTraffic="true"` from the manifest). If one host really needs HTTP, allow only that host in a `<domain-config>`.

**Verify:** Build a release APK, open an `http://` URL your app uses, and confirm the request fails with a cleartext error.

**IDs:** MASWE-0026 · MASVS-NETWORK-1 · MASTG-TEST-0235

**Read more:** [book §7.1](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/03-data-in-transit.md#71-the-baseline)

### AND-002: Release build is debuggable

**Severity:** critical · **Profiles:** MAS-L1 · **Confidence:** high · **Effort:** minutes

**Why it matters:** A debuggable release lets anyone with a USB cable attach a debugger and use `run-as` to read every private file the app has. It also turns on `debug-overrides`, which can switch off pinning.

**Fix:** Remove `android:debuggable="true"` from the main manifest and set `isDebuggable = false` (Groovy: `debuggable false`) in the `release` build type. Let the `debug` build type stay debuggable.

**Verify:** Build the release APK (or extract one from the bundle with bundletool) and run `aapt2 dump badging app-release.apk | grep application-debuggable`. It should print nothing.

**IDs:** MASWE-0063 · MASVS-RESILIENCE-4 · MASTG-TEST-0226 · MASTG-BEST-0007

**Read more:** [book §14.1](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/05-resilience.md#141-the-cheap-things-which-you-should-simply-do)

### AND-003: User-installed CAs are trusted in release

**Severity:** high · **Profiles:** MAS-L1 · **Confidence:** high · **Effort:** minutes

**Why it matters:** With `<certificates src="user"/>` outside `debug-overrides`, any certificate a user installs, such as a proxy's, can read and change the app's HTTPS traffic in release builds.

**Fix:** Remove `<certificates src="user"/>` from `base-config` and `domain-config`. If you need a proxy while developing, put it inside `<debug-overrides>`, which Android uses only in debuggable builds.

**Verify:** Install a proxy CA on a test phone, run the release build through the proxy, and confirm HTTPS requests fail.

**IDs:** MASWE-0027 · MASVS-NETWORK-1 · MASTG-TEST-0286

**Read more:** [book §7.1](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/03-data-in-transit.md#71-the-baseline)

### AND-004: WebView ignores TLS certificate errors

**Severity:** critical · **Profiles:** MAS-L1 · **Confidence:** high · **Effort:** minutes

**Why it matters:** Calling `proceed()` in `onReceivedSslError` turns off certificate checks for that WebView. Anyone on the network can then show their own page and read what the user types.

**Fix:** Call `handler.cancel()` in `onReceivedSslError` and never `handler.proceed()`. Fix the certificate on the server instead.

**Verify:** Point the WebView at a site with a bad certificate (for example through a proxy without its CA installed) and confirm the page doesn't load.

**IDs:** MASWE-0027 · MASVS-NETWORK-1 · MASTG-TEST-0284

**Read more:** [book §16.4](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/07-platform-surfaces-and-new-frontiers.md#164-loading-untrusted-content)

### AND-005: TrustManager or HostnameVerifier accepts everything

**Severity:** critical · **Profiles:** MAS-L1 · **Confidence:** high · **Effort:** hours

**Why it matters:** An empty `checkServerTrusted()` or a host-name check that always returns `true` turns off TLS server checks. Anyone on the same network can impersonate your server and read the traffic.

**Fix:** Delete the custom TrustManager and HostnameVerifier and use the platform defaults. If you need pinning, add a `<pin-set>` or OkHttp `CertificatePinner`, which run on top of normal validation.

**Verify:** Send the app's traffic through a proxy whose CA the phone doesn't trust and confirm every request fails.

**IDs:** MASWE-0027 · MASVS-NETWORK-1 · MASTG-TEST-0234 · MASTG-TEST-0282 · MASTG-TEST-0283

**Read more:** [book §7.1](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/03-data-in-transit.md#71-the-baseline)

### AND-006: OkHttp or SSLContext allows old TLS or plain HTTP

**Severity:** medium · **Profiles:** MAS-L1 · **Confidence:** medium · **Effort:** minutes

**Why it matters:** `ConnectionSpec.CLEARTEXT`, `COMPATIBLE_TLS`, or TLS 1.0/1.1 lets connections fall back to plain HTTP or to old protocol versions with known weaknesses.

**Fix:** Use `ConnectionSpec.MODERN_TLS` (TLS 1.3 and 1.2 only) and leave `ConnectionSpec.CLEARTEXT` out of the list. Request `SSLContext.getInstance("TLS")`, not `SSL` or `TLSv1`.

**Verify:** Check that an `http://` URL fails and that a server limited to TLS 1.1 is refused.

**IDs:** MASWE-0026 · MASVS-NETWORK-1 · MASTG-TEST-0217 · MASTG-TEST-0218

**Read more:** [book §7.1](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/03-data-in-transit.md#71-the-baseline)

### AND-007: No certificate pinning (needed for high-risk apps)

**Severity:** medium · **Profiles:** MAS-L2 · **Confidence:** medium · **Effort:** days · **Only for:** banking, identity, health, ecommerce-cards · **Reported in:** Hardening checklist

**Why it matters:** Without pinning, any CA in the system trust store can issue a certificate for your server, so a rogue or hacked CA can intercept the app's traffic. Apps that move money or hold health data are worth that extra protection.

**Fix:** Pin the SPKI of your CA's intermediate in `network_security_config.xml`, with a backup pin at a second CA and an expiration date. Write a rotation runbook before you ship it. Pin only if you can also run failure alerts, CT monitoring, and a protected kill switch (§8.7); if not, don't pin and rely on strict TLS plus CT (§8.9). In React Native, call `initializeSslPinning` (react-native-ssl-public-key-pinning) before the first request, or add the `<pin-set>` to the Android project.

**Verify:** Configure a wrong pin on a test build and confirm connections fail with a pin error. Then restore the real pins.

**Other apps:** Pinning is for apps that handle money, health data, identity credentials, or card numbers. For other apps the book recommends strict TLS plus Certificate Transparency monitoring: pinning adds outage risk for little gain, and if you can't update the pins securely, don't pin (§8.8). Enterprise apps: trust your private CA explicitly instead (§8.8).

**IDs:** MASWE-0028 · MASVS-NETWORK-2 · MASTG-TEST-0242

**Read more:** [book §8.8](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/03-data-in-transit.md#88-the-decision-by-application-type)

### AND-008: Pin set has no backup pin or no expiration date

**Severity:** medium · **Profiles:** MAS-L2 · **Confidence:** high · **Effort:** hours

**Why it matters:** With one pin and no backup, a routine key change locks every user on that build out of your server until they update. With no expiration, an app nobody updates stays broken forever.

**Fix:** Add a second pin for an intermediate at another CA (or a spare key you hold), and set `expiration` a little past the longest time you support a build. Set a reminder well before that date. With react-native-ssl-public-key-pinning, list two or more `publicKeyHashes` and an `expirationDate` for each host.

**Verify:** Read `network_security_config.xml` in the release APK and confirm each `<pin-set>` has two or more pins and a future `expiration`.

**IDs:** MASWE-0028 · MASVS-NETWORK-2 · MASTG-TEST-0243

**Read more:** [book §8.6](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/03-data-in-transit.md#86-where-the-pins-live-static-dynamic-and-hybrid)

### AND-009: Pinning or certificate trust depends on a BuildConfig flag

**Severity:** medium · **Profiles:** MAS-L1 · **Confidence:** medium · **Effort:** hours

**Why it matters:** A flag that relaxes security is a flag an attacker wants to flip. R8 doesn't always delete the relaxed branch, so it can survive in the release binary for someone to switch back on.

**Fix:** Configure pinning and trust the same way in every build. Put debug-only trust in `src/debug/` (for example a `network_security_config.xml` with `<debug-overrides>`) so the code doesn't exist in release.

**Verify:** Decompile the release APK and confirm the relaxed trust path isn't there.

**Read more:** [book §15.8](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/06-the-build-and-release-pipeline.md#158-build-configuration-in-code)

### AND-010: WebView can read local files

**Severity:** high · **Profiles:** MAS-L1 · **Confidence:** high · **Effort:** hours

**Why it matters:** If a WebView with file access loads a page an attacker can influence, that page can read the app's private files and send them out. A WebView that loads only web pages is reported as low.

**Fix:** Remove `allowFileAccess = true` and never enable `allowFileAccessFromFileURLs` or `allowUniversalAccessFromFileURLs`. Serve bundled HTML with `WebViewAssetLoader` over `https://appassets.androidplatform.net/`.

**Verify:** Load a test page that tries to fetch a `file:///data/data/<package>/` URL and confirm it's blocked.

**IDs:** MASWE-0034 · MASVS-PLATFORM-2 · MASTG-TEST-0250 · MASTG-TEST-0251 · MASTG-TEST-0252 · MASTG-TEST-0253

**Read more:** [book §16.3](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/07-platform-surfaces-and-new-frontiers.md#163-file-access-the-setting-nobody-remembers-changing)

### AND-011: WebView loads HTTP content inside HTTPS pages

**Severity:** medium · **Profiles:** MAS-L1 · **Confidence:** high · **Effort:** minutes

**Why it matters:** `MIXED_CONTENT_ALWAYS_ALLOW` lets an HTTPS page pull scripts and images over plain HTTP. Anyone on the network can replace those scripts and take over the page.

**Fix:** Remove the `mixedContentMode` line (or the `mixedContentMode` prop of a React Native WebView). Apps targeting API 21+ default to `MIXED_CONTENT_NEVER_ALLOW`, and react-native-webview defaults to "never". Serve every resource over HTTPS.

**Verify:** Load your pages in a debug build with WebView debugging on and confirm the console shows no mixed-content requests succeeding.

**Read more:** [book §16.3](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/07-platform-surfaces-and-new-frontiers.md#163-file-access-the-setting-nobody-remembers-changing)

### AND-012: JavaScript bridge is reachable from every frame

**Severity:** high · **Profiles:** MAS-L1 · **Confidence:** medium · **Effort:** hours

**Why it matters:** `addJavascriptInterface` exposes native methods to every frame in the WebView, including iframes and ads, with no origin check. Any script that runs there can call your code. A WebView that loads only fixed https or bundled pages is reported as medium.

**Fix:** Use `WebViewCompat.addWebMessageListener` with an allowlist of origins, and validate every message. If you must keep `addJavascriptInterface`, expose one narrow method and treat its input as untrusted.

**Verify:** Load a page with a third-party iframe and confirm the iframe can't reach the bridge.

**IDs:** MASWE-0033 · MASVS-PLATFORM-2 · MASTG-TEST-0334 · MASTG-BEST-0035

**Read more:** [book §16.2](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/07-platform-surfaces-and-new-frontiers.md#162-the-javascript-bridge-and-why-its-the-sharpest-edge)

### AND-013: WebView debugging is on in release

**Severity:** high · **Profiles:** MAS-L1 · **Confidence:** high · **Effort:** minutes

**Why it matters:** With WebView debugging on, anyone with the phone and a USB cable can open Chrome DevTools, read the page, change its content, and call your JavaScript bridge.

**Fix:** Tie debugging to the build type: `WebView.setWebContentsDebuggingEnabled(debuggable)`, where `debuggable` comes from `FLAG_DEBUGGABLE`. Never pass a plain `true`. In React Native, pass `webviewDebuggingEnabled={__DEV__}`.

**Verify:** Install the release build, open `chrome://inspect` on a computer, and confirm the app's WebViews aren't listed.

**IDs:** MASWE-0063 · MASVS-RESILIENCE-4 · MASTG-TEST-0227 · MASTG-BEST-0008

**Read more:** [book §16.6](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/07-platform-surfaces-and-new-frontiers.md#166-cleanup-and-hygiene)

### AND-014: WebView loads a URL from an intent or deep link

**Severity:** high · **Profiles:** MAS-L1 · **Confidence:** medium · **Effort:** hours

**Why it matters:** If a deep link or intent extra decides what the WebView loads, an attacker chooses the page that runs inside your app, with its cookies and any JavaScript bridge.

**Fix:** Parse the URL with `Uri.parse`, require `https`, and compare the parsed host with an exact allowlist before calling `loadUrl`. Check again in `shouldOverrideUrlLoading`.

**Verify:** Send the app a link that carries `https://evil.example/` as the URL parameter and confirm the WebView refuses it.

**IDs:** MASWE-0035 · MASVS-PLATFORM-2 · MASTG-TEST-0398 · MASTG-TEST-0400

**Read more:** [book §16.4](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/07-platform-surfaces-and-new-frontiers.md#164-loading-untrusted-content)

### AND-015: Exported component has no permission

**Severity:** high · **Profiles:** MAS-L1 · **Confidence:** manual · **Effort:** hours

**Why it matters:** Any app on the device can start an exported activity, service, receiver, or provider. Without a permission, a malicious app can skip your login screen or trigger the component's action directly. A custom action next to public intent filters, or a widget or media receiver, is reported as medium.

**Fix:** Set `android:exported="false"` unless other apps must reach the component. If they must, require a permission with `android:protectionLevel="signature"` and validate every input.

**Verify:** Run `adb shell am start -n <package>/<component>` (or `am startservice`, `am broadcast`) from a shell and confirm it's refused.

**IDs:** MASWE-0018 · MASVS-AUTH-1 · MASTG-TEST-0364 · MASTG-TEST-0365 · MASTG-TEST-0366 · MASTG-TEST-0355

**Read more:** [book §17.1](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/07-platform-surfaces-and-new-frontiers.md#171-android-app-components-and-the-word-exported)

### AND-016: FileProvider shares too much of the filesystem

**Severity:** high · **Profiles:** MAS-L1 · **Confidence:** high · **Effort:** minutes

**Why it matters:** `<root-path>` or `path="."` in `file_paths.xml` lets a caller ask for files outside the folder you meant to share, including your databases and preferences. External storage paths are reported as medium: those files aren't private to the app anyway.

**Fix:** Scope each entry in `file_paths.xml` to the narrowest folder that works, such as `<cache-path name="shared_exports" path="exports/" />`. Remove `<root-path>`. Grant read, not write, unless the recipient must write.

**Verify:** Ask the provider for a URI that points at `../databases/` and confirm it fails.

**IDs:** MASWE-0018 · MASVS-AUTH-1 · MASTG-TEST-0357

**Read more:** [book §17.4](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/07-platform-surfaces-and-new-frontiers.md#174-content-providers)

### AND-017: App starts an Intent it received from another app

**Severity:** high · **Profiles:** MAS-L1 · **Confidence:** medium · **Effort:** hours

**Why it matters:** An Intent pulled out of another Intent's extras runs as your app. It can open your non-exported screens or hand out access to your private files.

**Fix:** Don't forward nested Intents. If you must, run them through AndroidX `IntentSanitizer`, allowing only the component and extras you expect.

**Verify:** From a test app, send an Intent whose extra points at one of your non-exported activities and confirm it doesn't open.

**IDs:** MASWE-0032 · MASVS-PLATFORM-1

**Read more:** [book §17.2](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/07-platform-surfaces-and-new-frontiers.md#172-intents-explicit-versus-implicit)

### AND-018: Mutable PendingIntent

**Severity:** medium · **Profiles:** MAS-L1 · **Confidence:** medium · **Effort:** minutes

**Why it matters:** A mutable `PendingIntent` lets the app that receives it fill in the destination or data. With an implicit base Intent, it can redirect the Intent, which then runs with your app's identity and permissions.

**Fix:** Use `PendingIntent.FLAG_IMMUTABLE` with an explicit Intent. Keep `FLAG_MUTABLE` only where you need it, such as inline replies, and make the base Intent explicit there.

**Verify:** Check each place that creates a `PendingIntent` and confirm it's immutable or has an explicit component.

**IDs:** MASWE-0032 · MASVS-PLATFORM-1 · MASTG-TEST-0381 · MASTG-BEST-0063

**Read more:** [book §17.3](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/07-platform-surfaces-and-new-frontiers.md#173-pendingintent-the-one-that-looks-harmless)

### AND-019: App Link is not verified

**Severity:** medium · **Profiles:** MAS-L1 · **Confidence:** medium · **Effort:** hours

**Why it matters:** Without `android:autoVerify="true"`, Android doesn't confirm that your domain belongs to your app. Another app can claim the same links, or Android opens them in the browser.

**Fix:** Add `android:autoVerify="true"` to the `https` intent filter and host `/.well-known/assetlinks.json` with your app signing certificate fingerprint.

**Verify:** Run `adb shell pm get-app-links <package>` on a Play install and confirm each domain shows `verified`.

**IDs:** MASWE-0029 · MASVS-PLATFORM-1 · MASTG-TEST-0393 · MASTG-BEST-0070

**Read more:** [book §17.5](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/07-platform-surfaces-and-new-frontiers.md#175-deep-links-and-the-verification-that-makes-them-safe)

### AND-020: SQL query built by joining strings

**Severity:** high · **Profiles:** MAS-L1 · **Confidence:** medium · **Effort:** hours

**Why it matters:** When part of a SQL string comes from input, that input can change the query: read other users' rows, or the whole database through a content provider. One-time migrations over values the app owns aren't reported.

**Fix:** Use `?` placeholders and pass values as `selectionArgs`, or Room `@Query` with bound parameters. Allowlist column names and sort orders.

**Verify:** Pass `' OR '1'='1` into the code path and confirm it's treated as plain text.

**IDs:** MASWE-0050 · MASVS-CODE-4 · MASTG-TEST-0339

**Read more:** [book §19.3](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/07-platform-surfaces-and-new-frontiers.md#193-injection-the-shape-of-the-bug)

### AND-021: Backup is on with no exclusion rules

**Severity:** medium · **Profiles:** MAS-L1 · **Confidence:** high · **Effort:** hours

**Why it matters:** Android Auto Backup copies the app's files, including tokens and databases, to cloud storage and to new phones. Keystore keys are never backed up, so restored ciphertext can also crash the app.

**Fix:** Add `android:dataExtractionRules` (Android 12+) and `android:fullBackupContent` (Android 11 and lower) that exclude secrets and their keysets, in both `<cloud-backup>` and `<device-transfer>`. In a managed Expo app, set `android.allowBackup` to false in app.json, or add the rules through a config plugin.

**Verify:** Run `adb shell bmgr backupnow <package>` over an encrypted local transport, reinstall, and confirm the excluded files are gone after the restore.

**IDs:** MASWE-0006 · MASVS-STORAGE-2 · MASTG-TEST-0216 · MASTG-TEST-0262

**Read more:** [book §6.5](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/02-data-at-rest.md#65-the-leaks-that-are-not-about-encryption)

### AND-022: Deprecated EncryptedSharedPreferences (Jetpack Security)

**Severity:** medium · **Profiles:** MAS-L1 · **Confidence:** high · **Effort:** days

**Why it matters:** Google deprecated every API in `androidx.security:security-crypto` in 2025, and it gets no fixes. It's also known for keyset-corruption crashes on some devices.

**Fix:** If the stored values aren't secrets (flags, UI state), move them to plain DataStore or SharedPreferences: the sandbox already protects them (§6.4). For tokens and credentials, use DataStore, Tink, and an Android Keystore master key (`androidx.datastore:datastore-tink`). Migrate with `SharedPreferencesMigration`, then delete the old file and Keystore alias.

**Verify:** Confirm the dependency is gone from the build and that `files/datastore/` holds only binary ciphertext.

**IDs:** MASWE-0046 · MASVS-CODE-3

**Read more:** [book §6.1](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/02-data-at-rest.md#61-encryptedsharedpreferences-is-dead)

### AND-023: End-of-life SQLCipher package

**Severity:** medium · **Profiles:** MAS-L1 · **Confidence:** high · **Effort:** hours

**Why it matters:** `net.zetetic:android-database-sqlcipher` reached end of life in 2023 and gets no security fixes. Its open-source build won't get the 16 KB page-size support Play will require.

**Fix:** Switch to `net.zetetic:sqlcipher-android` (package `net.zetetic.database.sqlcipher`). Use `SupportOpenHelperFactory` with Room 2 or `SQLCipherDriver` with Room 3.

**Verify:** Confirm the old coordinates and `net.sqlcipher` imports are gone, then open an existing database to check the migration.

**Read more:** [book §6.7](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/02-data-at-rest.md#67-encrypting-a-local-database)

### AND-024: Tink may silently store its keyset in plain text

**Severity:** medium · **Profiles:** MAS-L2 · **Confidence:** medium · **Effort:** minutes

**Why it matters:** When the Android Keystore fails its self-test, Tink's `AndroidKeysetManager` stores the keyset unencrypted and only logs a warning. Your encrypted data is then protected by a key anyone with file access can read.

**Fix:** After `build()`, check `manager.isUsingKeystore` and record the result (for example in security telemetry), so you know when the fallback happens.

**Verify:** Log `isUsingKeystore` in a debug build on your test devices and confirm it's `true` where you expect hardware backing.

**Read more:** [book §6.3](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/02-data-at-rest.md#63-what-to-use-instead)

### AND-025: Biometric prompt is not tied to a key

**Severity:** high · **Profiles:** MAS-L2 · **Confidence:** medium · **Effort:** days

**Why it matters:** Without a `CryptoObject`, the biometric prompt only returns success or failure. A Frida hook can call your success callback with no fingerprint at all.

**Fix:** Pass a `CryptoObject` wrapping a Keystore key created with `setUserAuthenticationRequired(true)`, and do the protected work (sign or decrypt) with `result.cryptoObject` in the success callback.

**Verify:** Run a biometric-bypass Frida script against a debug build and confirm the protected action still fails.

**IDs:** MASWE-0020 · MASVS-AUTH-2 · MASTG-TEST-0327 · MASTG-BEST-0036

**Read more:** [book §11.1](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/04-proving-who-is-calling.md#111-decorative-versus-real)

### AND-026: Biometric key survives a new fingerprint or face

**Severity:** high · **Profiles:** MAS-L2 · **Confidence:** medium · **Effort:** hours

**Why it matters:** Someone who knows the phone's PIN can add their own fingerprint. If the key isn't invalidated on new enrollment, your app then accepts them.

**Fix:** Keep `setInvalidatedByBiometricEnrollment(true)` (the default), use `setUserAuthenticationParameters(0, KeyProperties.AUTH_BIOMETRIC_STRONG)`, and don't add `AUTH_DEVICE_CREDENTIAL` or a validity window to the key.

**Verify:** Add a new fingerprint on a test phone and confirm using the key throws `KeyPermanentlyInvalidatedException`.

**IDs:** MASWE-0022 · MASVS-AUTH-2 · MASTG-TEST-0328 · MASTG-TEST-0330

**Read more:** [book §11.3](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/04-proving-who-is-calling.md#113-the-enrollment-problem-nobody-thinks-about)

### AND-027: R8 is off in the release build

**Severity:** medium · **Profiles:** MAS-L1 · **Confidence:** high · **Effort:** hours

**Why it matters:** Without R8, the release build keeps every class and method name, which hands a reverse engineer a map of your code, and ships unused code you never meant to include.

**Fix:** Set `isMinifyEnabled = true` and `isShrinkResources = true` in the `release` build type, with `proguard-android-optimize.txt`. Keep only the keep rules reflection needs. In React Native, set `def enableProguardInReleaseBuilds = true` in android/app/build.gradle.

**Verify:** Decompile the release APK with jadx and confirm your class names are shortened.

**IDs:** MASWE-0059 · MASVS-RESILIENCE-3 · MASTG-TEST-0368

**Read more:** [book §14.1](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/05-resilience.md#141-the-cheap-things-which-you-should-simply-do)

### AND-028: targetSdk is below Google Play's requirement

**Severity:** medium · **Profiles:** MAS-L1 · **Confidence:** high · **Effort:** days

**Why it matters:** Google Play requires new apps and updates to target API 36. Each newer target turns on platform protections that older targets don't get, such as a required PendingIntent mutability flag (API 31) and a block on mutable implicit PendingIntents (API 34).

**Fix:** Raise `targetSdk` to 36 or later, then test the behavior changes for each version you skipped.

**Verify:** Run `aapt2 dump badging app-release.apk | grep targetSdkVersion` and confirm it shows 36 or more.

**IDs:** MASWE-0042 · MASVS-CODE-1

**Read more:** [book §19.6](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/07-platform-surfaces-and-new-frontiers.md#196-free-compiler-protections-and-platform-currency)

### AND-029: minSdk is below 24

**Severity:** low · **Profiles:** MAS-L1 · **Confidence:** high · **Effort:** hours

**Why it matters:** On Android 6 and older (below API 24), every app trusts user-installed CAs by default, so a proxy certificate can read your traffic. Old API levels also lack newer security features.

**Fix:** Raise `minSdk` to at least 24. Android ignores the network security config below API 24, so it can't protect those devices. If you must support them, use a TrustManager that trusts only system CAs (or OkHttp `CertificatePinner` in a high-risk app), or accept the risk for those users.

**Verify:** Run `aapt2 dump badging app-release.apk | grep sdkVersion` and confirm it shows 24 or more.

**IDs:** MASWE-0041 · MASVS-CODE-1 · MASTG-TEST-0245 · MASTG-TEST-0285 · MASTG-BEST-0010

**Read more:** [book §19.6](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/07-platform-surfaces-and-new-frontiers.md#196-free-compiler-protections-and-platform-currency)

### AND-030: HTTP bodies are logged in every build

**Severity:** medium · **Profiles:** MAS-L1 · **Confidence:** medium · **Effort:** minutes

**Why it matters:** `HttpLoggingInterceptor.Level.BODY` writes full requests and responses, including tokens and personal data, to logcat, where bug reports and crash reporters can collect them.

**Fix:** Use `Level.BODY` only when `BuildConfig.DEBUG` is true and `Level.NONE` otherwise, or add the interceptor only in debug builds.

**Verify:** Run the release build, sign in, and watch `adb logcat --pid=$(adb shell pidof -s <package>)`. No request bodies or tokens should appear.

**IDs:** MASWE-0005 · MASVS-STORAGE-2 · MASTG-TEST-0203 · MASTG-TEST-0231

**Read more:** [book §6.5](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/02-data-at-rest.md#65-the-leaks-that-are-not-about-encryption)

### AND-031: Code is loaded at runtime

**Severity:** high · **Profiles:** MAS-L1 · **Confidence:** manual · **Effort:** days

**Why it matters:** Code loaded with `DexClassLoader` or `System.load` from outside your signed package isn't covered by your signature. Whoever can replace that file controls your app, and Google Play forbids downloading executable code.

**Fix:** Ship all code inside the signed app. If you must load a file, load it only from a read-only path inside your own package.

**Verify:** Check where each loaded file comes from and confirm none is downloaded or writable by other code.

**IDs:** MASWE-0049 · MASVS-CODE-4

**Read more:** [book §19.5](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/07-platform-surfaces-and-new-frontiers.md#195-dynamic-code-loading)

### AND-032: Java deserialization with ObjectInputStream

**Severity:** high · **Profiles:** MAS-L1 · **Confidence:** manual · **Effort:** hours

**Why it matters:** `ObjectInputStream` builds whatever classes the bytes name. If the data comes from another app, a file, or the network, crafted bytes can construct objects you never intended and sometimes run code. A class-allowlist subclass and in-memory deep copies aren't reported; reading an app file is medium.

**Fix:** Parse into declared types instead: JSON with `kotlinx.serialization`, or Protocol Buffers. For intent extras, use the typed `IntentCompat.getParcelableExtra(intent, name, Class)`.

**Verify:** Feed the decoder a payload that names a class you didn't expect and confirm it's rejected.

**IDs:** MASWE-0050 · MASVS-CODE-4 · MASTG-TEST-0337

**Read more:** [book §19.4](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/07-platform-surfaces-and-new-frontiers.md#194-deserialization)

### AND-033: App requests sensitive permissions

**Severity:** info · **Profiles:** MAS-P · **Confidence:** manual · **Effort:** hours

**Why it matters:** Each sensitive permission is attack surface and a privacy promise to users. Third-party SDKs can use it too, and Play restricts some of them, such as broad photo access. This is the app's merged inventory to review.

**Fix:** Ask only for what a feature needs, at the point of use, with a rationale. Prefer narrower options: the photo picker, approximate location, or `READ_MEDIA_VISUAL_USER_SELECTED`.

**Verify:** Check the merged manifest in Android Studio and confirm every sensitive permission maps to a feature.

**IDs:** MASWE-0066 · MASVS-PRIVACY-1 · MASTG-TEST-0254

**Read more:** [book §18.1](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/07-platform-surfaces-and-new-frontiers.md#181-permissions-ask-for-less-later-and-explain-why)

### AND-034: Token or password stored in plain SharedPreferences or DataStore

**Severity:** medium · **Profiles:** MAS-L2 · **Confidence:** manual · **Effort:** hours

**Why it matters:** SharedPreferences and DataStore write plain files in the app's private folder. They are copied into backups and are readable by anyone with root or physical access to the device, so a long-lived token there can be lifted and replayed.

**Fix:** Keep short-lived tokens in memory. Encrypt long-lived tokens before storing them, with a key held in the Android Keystore: for example Tink's AEAD with an `AndroidKeysetManager` master key, checking `isUsingKeystore()`. Keep only non-secret settings in plain preferences.

**Verify:** Sign in on an emulator, then run `adb shell run-as <package> ls -R shared_prefs files/datastore` and print each file with `cat`. Confirm no token or password appears in readable form.

**IDs:** MASWE-0001 · MASVS-STORAGE-1 · MASTG-TEST-0287 · MASTG-TEST-0305

**Read more:** [book §6.4](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/02-data-at-rest.md#64-the-uncomfortable-question-nobody-asked)

### AND-035: Network security config allows plain HTTP for a domain

**Severity:** high · **Profiles:** MAS-L1 · **Confidence:** high · **Effort:** minutes

**Why it matters:** A `domain-config` with `cleartextTrafficPermitted="true"` lets the app talk to that host over plain HTTP, so anyone on the network path can read or change the traffic, including tokens sent to it.

**Fix:** Remove the `domain-config` or set `cleartextTrafficPermitted="false"`. If a legacy host needs HTTP, put it behind HTTPS on your side first.

**Verify:** Build a release APK, call the listed host over `http://`, and confirm the request fails with a cleartext error.

**IDs:** MASWE-0026 · MASVS-NETWORK-1 · MASTG-TEST-0235

**Read more:** [book §7.1](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/03-data-in-transit.md#71-the-baseline)

### AND-036: Backup rules don't keep sensitive data out of device-to-device transfer

**Severity:** medium · **Profiles:** MAS-L1 · **Confidence:** high · **Effort:** minutes

**Why it matters:** Android 12+ copies app files to a new phone through device-to-device transfer, which only `<device-transfer>` in `dataExtractionRules` controls. A cloud-backup exclusion, or `allowBackup="false"` on some devices, doesn't keep a file out of that copy.

**Fix:** Add `android:dataExtractionRules` with matching `<exclude>` entries in both `<cloud-backup>` and `<device-transfer>` for tokens, keysets and databases.

**Verify:** Check that the rules file excludes the same files in both sections, then move the app to a second phone with the setup wizard and confirm the excluded files are absent (`adb shell run-as <package> ls -R`).

**IDs:** MASWE-0006 · MASVS-STORAGE-2 · MASTG-TEST-0262 · MASTG-BEST-0004

**Read more:** [book §6.5](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/02-data-at-rest.md#65-the-leaks-that-are-not-about-encryption)

### AND-037: Debug tool library ships in the release build

**Severity:** high · **Profiles:** MAS-L1 · **Confidence:** high · **Effort:** minutes

**Why it matters:** Tools such as Stetho, Flipper, Chucker and LeakCanary expose the app's databases, preferences, network traffic or heap dumps. Added with `implementation`, they ship to every user, and anyone holding the phone can read that data.

**Fix:** Use `debugImplementation` (or the library's `-no-op` artifact with `releaseImplementation`) and start the tool from code in `src/debug/`.

**Verify:** Run `./gradlew :app:dependencies --configuration releaseRuntimeClasspath` and confirm none of these libraries appear.

**IDs:** MASWE-0063 · MASVS-RESILIENCE-4 · MASTG-BEST-0007

**Read more:** [book §14.1](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/05-resilience.md#141-the-cheap-things-which-you-should-simply-do)

### AND-038: Release build turns on native debugging or is marked test-only

**Severity:** high · **Profiles:** MAS-L1 · **Confidence:** high · **Effort:** minutes

**Why it matters:** `jniDebuggable` lets a debugger attach to the app's native code, `testCoverageEnabled` ships coverage instrumentation, and `android:testOnly="true"` marks the APK as a test build. None of these belong in a build users install.

**Fix:** Remove these settings from release build types and the main manifest. Keep native debugging in `debug {}` only.

**Verify:** Run `aapt2 dump badging app-release.apk` and confirm it shows no `testOnly` flag, and check that the release build type sets none of these options.

**IDs:** MASWE-0063 · MASVS-RESILIENCE-4 · MASTG-TEST-0226 · MASTG-BEST-0007

**Read more:** [book §14.1](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/05-resilience.md#141-the-cheap-things-which-you-should-simply-do)

### AND-039: Timber logs everything in release builds

**Severity:** medium · **Profiles:** MAS-L1 · **Confidence:** high · **Effort:** minutes

**Why it matters:** `Timber.DebugTree` sends every log call to logcat. Planted in release, any debug log of a request, token or user field is readable over adb and in bug reports.

**Fix:** Plant `DebugTree` only under `if (BuildConfig.DEBUG)`. In release, plant a tree that keeps only warnings and errors and never logs request data.

**Verify:** Install the release build, sign in, and confirm `adb logcat --pid=$(adb shell pidof <package>)` shows no debug or info lines from the app.

**IDs:** MASWE-0005 · MASVS-STORAGE-2 · MASTG-TEST-0231 · MASTG-BEST-0002

**Read more:** [book §6.6](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/02-data-at-rest.md#66-how-to-implement-it)

### AND-040: WebView Safe Browsing is turned off

**Severity:** medium · **Profiles:** MAS-L1 · **Confidence:** high · **Effort:** minutes

**Why it matters:** Safe Browsing warns users before a WebView loads a known phishing or malware page. Turning it off removes that check for every page the WebView shows, including links from messages or ads.

**Fix:** Remove the `EnableSafeBrowsing` meta-data set to false and any `setSafeBrowsingEnabled(false)` call. Safe Browsing is on by default.

**Verify:** Load `chrome://safe-browsing/match?type=malware` in the WebView and confirm the warning page appears.

**IDs:** MASWE-0035 · MASVS-PLATFORM-2 · MASTG-TEST-0399

**Read more:** [book §16.3](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/07-platform-surfaces-and-new-frontiers.md#163-file-access-the-setting-nobody-remembers-changing)

### AND-041: Keystore key accepts caller-chosen IVs

**Severity:** high · **Profiles:** MAS-L1 · **Confidence:** high · **Effort:** hours

**Why it matters:** By default a Keystore key refuses an IV the caller supplies and generates a fresh one. `setRandomizedEncryptionRequired(false)` removes that guard, so a reused IV with AES-GCM can reveal plaintext and allow forgeries.

**Fix:** Remove the call. Let the Keystore pick the IV, then store `cipher.iv` next to the ciphertext.

**Verify:** Encrypt the same value twice and confirm the IVs and the ciphertexts differ.

**IDs:** MASWE-0007 · MASVS-CRYPTO-1 · MASTG-TEST-0309

**Read more:** [book §6.6](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/02-data-at-rest.md#66-how-to-implement-it)

### AND-042: App reads a hardware identifier

**Severity:** low · **Profiles:** MAS-P · **Confidence:** high · **Effort:** hours

**Why it matters:** IMEI, serial number, MAC address and ANDROID_ID identify the device across apps or survive a reset of the advertising ID. Using them to profile users breaks store policy and takes away the user's ability to reset tracking.

**Fix:** Use a server-generated or app-scoped ID (the app set ID, or a UUID you store), and the advertising ID only with consent.

**Verify:** Search the release code for these APIs and confirm each remaining use has a purpose other than tracking.

**IDs:** MASWE-0068 · MASVS-PRIVACY-2

**Read more:** [book §18.2](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/07-platform-surfaces-and-new-frontiers.md#182-identifiers-and-tracking)

### AND-043: File name from another app is used as a path (Dirty Stream)

**Severity:** high · **Profiles:** MAS-L1 · **Confidence:** medium · **Effort:** hours

**Why it matters:** A content provider controls the display name it returns. If the app saves a shared file under that name, a name such as `../shared_prefs/x.xml` overwrites the app's own files, which can leak tokens or run attacker code.

**Fix:** Ignore the supplied name and generate your own, or keep only `File(name).name`, and check that the canonical path stays inside your directory.

**Verify:** Share a file from a test provider whose display name is `../../shared_prefs/evil.xml` and confirm nothing is written outside the target directory.

**IDs:** MASWE-0050 · MASVS-CODE-4 · MASTG-BEST-0057

**Read more:** [book §17.2](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/07-platform-surfaces-and-new-frontiers.md#172-intents-explicit-versus-implicit)

### AND-044: SafetyNet Attestation is still called

**Severity:** high · **Profiles:** MAS-L1 · **Confidence:** high · **Effort:** days

**Why it matters:** Google shut down SafetyNet Attestation in January 2025. Calls now fail, so any login, payment or fraud decision that relies on its verdict either breaks or is skipped.

**Fix:** Migrate to Play Integrity standard requests and verify the verdict on your server (§9.6).

**Verify:** Confirm no code path calls `SafetyNet.getClient(...).attest(` and that the server checks Play Integrity verdicts instead.

**IDs:** MASWE-0046 · MASVS-CODE-3

**Read more:** [book Chapter 9](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/04-proving-who-is-calling.md#chapter-9-play-integrity--what-it-proves-and-what-it-does-not)

### AND-045: App never blocks screenshots or the recents thumbnail

**Severity:** medium · **Profiles:** MAS-L2 · **Confidence:** high · **Effort:** hours · **Reported in:** Hardening checklist

**Why it matters:** Without `FLAG_SECURE`, screenshots, screen recording, casting and the recents-screen thumbnail capture whatever is on screen, including balances, card numbers and one-time codes.

**Fix:** Set `FLAG_SECURE` on screens that show account data or codes, and `SecureFlagPolicy.SecureOn` on Compose dialogs that show secrets. In React Native, use expo-screen-capture (`preventScreenCaptureAsync`) or react-native-capture-protection on those screens.

**Verify:** Open a sensitive screen, take a screenshot and open the recents screen; confirm both show a blank or blocked view.

**IDs:** MASWE-0038 · MASVS-PLATFORM-3 · MASTG-TEST-0291 · MASTG-BEST-0014 · MASTG-BEST-0016

**Read more:** [book §6.5](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/02-data-at-rest.md#65-the-leaks-that-are-not-about-encryption)

### AND-046: App has no overlay (tapjacking) protection

**Severity:** medium · **Profiles:** MAS-L2 · **Confidence:** high · **Effort:** hours · **Only for:** banking, identity, health, ecommerce-cards, device-control · **Reported in:** Hardening checklist

**Why it matters:** Android 12+ blocks touches through most full-screen overlays from other apps, but not a partial overlay that covers everything except your button. A malicious overlay can then trick the user into approving a transfer or a permission.

**Fix:** On sensitive screens, call `window.setHideOverlayWindows(true)` (API 31+, with the `HIDE_OVERLAY_WINDOWS` permission) and set `filterTouchesWhenObscured` on confirm and pay buttons. In React Native, set it in MainActivity (bare app) or through a config plugin (Expo).

**Verify:** Run a test app that draws a partial overlay over the confirm button and confirm the tap is ignored or the overlay is hidden.

**Other apps:** Overlay tricks matter where one tap moves money, shares health or identity data, or controls a device.

**IDs:** MASWE-0039 · MASVS-PLATFORM-3 · MASTG-TEST-0340 · MASTG-BEST-0040

**Read more:** [book §17.6](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/07-platform-surfaces-and-new-frontiers.md#176-the-other-channels-people-forget)

### AND-047: R8 keep rules undo obfuscation

**Severity:** medium · **Profiles:** MAS-R · **Confidence:** high · **Effort:** hours

**Why it matters:** R8 renames classes so the release build is harder to read. `-dontobfuscate`, a keep rule for every class, or keep rules for your security checks put the readable names back and show an attacker which code to patch.

**Fix:** Remove broad and security-class keep rules. Keep only what reflection or serialization reaches, by exact name or annotation.

**Verify:** Open the release APK in jadx and confirm your packages and your root or tamper checks have obfuscated names.

**IDs:** MASWE-0059 · MASVS-RESILIENCE-3 · MASTG-TEST-0368 · MASTG-BEST-0029

**Read more:** [book §15.8](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/06-the-build-and-release-pipeline.md#158-build-configuration-in-code)

### AND-048: Play Integrity is not integrated

**Severity:** medium · **Profiles:** MAS-R · **Confidence:** high · **Effort:** days · **Reported in:** Hardening checklist

**Why it matters:** Without Play Integrity the backend can't tell a request from your genuine app on a genuine device from one sent by a modified APK, an emulator farm or a script.

**Fix:** Request a standard Play Integrity token for sensitive actions and decide on the server (§9.3, §12.2). In React Native, use @react-native-firebase/app-check with the Play Integrity provider, or react-native-device-attest.

**Verify:** Send a sensitive request from a re-signed build and confirm the server rejects it or lowers its trust score.

**IDs:** MASWE-0056 · MASVS-RESILIENCE-2

**Read more:** [book §9.6](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/04-proving-who-is-calling.md#96-how-to-implement-it)

### AND-049: Keystore key may both encrypt and sign

**Severity:** low · **Profiles:** MAS-L1 · **Confidence:** high · **Effort:** hours

**Why it matters:** A key used for both encryption and signatures (or key wrapping) links the two uses: a weakness in one can forge or decrypt in the other. Each key should have one job.

**Fix:** Create one Keystore key per role: one with `PURPOSE_ENCRYPT or PURPOSE_DECRYPT`, another with `PURPOSE_SIGN or PURPOSE_VERIFY`.

**Verify:** List each `KeyGenParameterSpec.Builder` and confirm its purposes are either encryption or signing, not both.

**IDs:** MASWE-0007 · MASVS-CRYPTO-1 · MASTG-TEST-0307

**Read more:** [book Chapter 0.2](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/00-foundations.md#chapter-02-cryptography-you-actually-need)

### AND-050: Crypto call names an explicit provider

**Severity:** low · **Profiles:** MAS-L1 · **Confidence:** high · **Effort:** minutes

**Why it matters:** Naming a provider such as "BC" ties the app to a bundled or deprecated implementation that Android doesn't update, and Android 9 removed several of them. The platform's default provider gets security fixes.

**Fix:** Drop the provider argument, or use "AndroidKeyStore" for Keystore keys. Don't install Bouncy Castle as a global provider.

**Verify:** Search for two-argument `getInstance(` calls and `Security.addProvider`, and confirm only AndroidKeyStore or Conscrypt remain.

**IDs:** MASWE-0007 · MASVS-CRYPTO-1 · MASTG-TEST-0312 · MASTG-BEST-0020

**Read more:** [book Chapter 0.2](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/00-foundations.md#chapter-02-cryptography-you-actually-need)

### AND-051: Biometric prompt accepts weak (Class 2) biometrics

**Severity:** medium · **Profiles:** MAS-L2 · **Confidence:** high · **Effort:** minutes

**Why it matters:** Class 2 biometrics, such as many face unlocks, are easier to spoof and can't unlock a Keystore key. A prompt that accepts them is a boolean check, not proof that the owner is present.

**Fix:** Allow `BIOMETRIC_STRONG` and pass a `CryptoObject` so a Keystore key does the gating.

**Verify:** On a device with Class 2 face unlock, confirm the sensitive prompt asks for a Class 3 biometric or the device credential instead.

**IDs:** MASWE-0020 · MASVS-AUTH-2 · MASTG-TEST-0327

**Read more:** [book §11.2](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/04-proving-who-is-calling.md#112-biometric-classes-and-why-class-3-matters)

### AND-052: Biometric prompt doesn't require explicit confirmation

**Severity:** low · **Profiles:** MAS-L2 · **Confidence:** high · **Effort:** minutes · **Only for:** banking, identity, ecommerce-cards

**Why it matters:** With `setConfirmationRequired(false)`, a passive biometric such as face unlock approves the action as soon as the phone sees the user's face, without a deliberate tap. For payments, that means approvals the user didn't intend.

**Fix:** Remove the call (the default is `true`) on prompts that approve payments, transfers or other one-way actions.

**Verify:** Trigger the payment prompt with face unlock and confirm it waits for a confirm tap.

**Other apps:** Explicit confirmation matters for prompts that approve payments or identity actions.

**IDs:** MASWE-0020 · MASVS-AUTH-2 · MASTG-TEST-0329 · MASTG-BEST-0038

**Read more:** [book §11.4](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/04-proving-who-is-calling.md#114-fallbacks-and-the-tension-inside-them)

### AND-053: Screen-capture protection is switched off

**Severity:** medium · **Profiles:** MAS-L2 · **Confidence:** medium · **Effort:** minutes

**Why it matters:** Clearing `FLAG_SECURE`, using `SecureFlagPolicy.SecureOff`, or turning the recents screenshot back on lets screenshots, recordings and the recents thumbnail capture that screen. That's a leak when the screen shows account data or codes.

**Fix:** Keep `FLAG_SECURE` on every screen that shows secrets, and clear it only on screens that don't.

**Verify:** Open each screen where the flag is cleared and confirm it never shows balances, card data or codes.

**IDs:** MASWE-0038 · MASVS-PLATFORM-3 · MASTG-TEST-0291 · MASTG-TEST-0294

**Read more:** [book §6.5](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/02-data-at-rest.md#65-the-leaks-that-are-not-about-encryption)

### AND-054: Implicit Intent carries a token or password

**Severity:** high · **Profiles:** MAS-L1 · **Confidence:** medium · **Effort:** hours

**Why it matters:** An implicit Intent goes to whichever app has a matching filter. Extras such as a token, password or one-time code are readable by that app, which can be one the user installed by mistake.

**Fix:** Make the Intent explicit with `setPackage(packageName)` or a component, and don't put credentials in extras.

**Verify:** Install a test app with a matching intent filter and confirm it doesn't receive the Intent or its extras.

**IDs:** MASWE-0032 · MASVS-PLATFORM-1 · MASTG-TEST-0374 · MASTG-BEST-0056

**Read more:** [book §17.2](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/07-platform-surfaces-and-new-frontiers.md#172-intents-explicit-versus-implicit)

### AND-055: App-internal action is sent as an implicit Intent

**Severity:** medium · **Profiles:** MAS-L1 · **Confidence:** medium · **Effort:** hours

**Why it matters:** An action meant for the app's own components, sent without a package or component, reaches any app that declares the same action. That app can read the extras or answer in place of yours.

**Fix:** Call `intent.setPackage(packageName)` or use an explicit component. For broadcasts inside the app, also name a signature permission.

**Verify:** Install a test app with a filter for the action and confirm it never receives the Intent.

**IDs:** MASWE-0032 · MASVS-PLATFORM-1 · MASTG-TEST-0372 · MASTG-BEST-0056

**Read more:** [book §17.2](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/07-platform-surfaces-and-new-frontiers.md#172-intents-explicit-versus-implicit)

### AND-056: Receiver registered in code is exported

**Severity:** medium · **Profiles:** MAS-L1 · **Confidence:** high · **Effort:** minutes

**Why it matters:** A receiver registered with `RECEIVER_EXPORTED`, or without a flag below targetSdk 34, accepts broadcasts from every app. Any app can then trigger the receiver's action or feed it fake data.

**Fix:** Use `ContextCompat.registerReceiver(context, receiver, filter, ContextCompat.RECEIVER_NOT_EXPORTED)`, or pass a signature permission if your other apps must send it.

**Verify:** Send the action with `adb shell am broadcast -a <action>` and confirm the receiver doesn't run.

**IDs:** MASWE-0018 · MASVS-AUTH-1 · MASTG-TEST-0366 · MASTG-BEST-0052

**Read more:** [book §17.1](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/07-platform-surfaces-and-new-frontiers.md#171-android-app-components-and-the-word-exported)

### AND-057: Content provider grants URI access to every path

**Severity:** high · **Profiles:** MAS-L1 · **Confidence:** high · **Effort:** minutes

**Why it matters:** `<grant-uri-permission>` with `path="/"` or `pathPattern=".*"` lets the app hand out temporary access to any URI the provider serves. One grant meant for a single file can expose all of the provider's data.

**Fix:** Grant only specific paths, or share files through FileProvider with narrow `file_paths.xml` entries.

**Verify:** Grant a URI for one item to a test app and confirm it can't read other paths from the provider.

**IDs:** MASWE-0018 · MASVS-AUTH-1 · MASTG-TEST-0357

**Read more:** [book §17.4](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/07-platform-surfaces-and-new-frontiers.md#174-content-providers)

### AND-058: Provider protects reads but not writes

**Severity:** high · **Profiles:** MAS-L1 · **Confidence:** high · **Effort:** hours

**Why it matters:** With only `android:readPermission`, `insert`, `update` and `delete` stay open to every app. A malicious app can change or wipe the provider's data even though it can't read it.

**Fix:** Add `android:writePermission` with a `signature` protection level, or remove the write methods.

**Verify:** Run `adb shell content insert --uri content://<authority>/<path> --bind x:s:y` and confirm it's refused.

**IDs:** MASWE-0018 · MASVS-AUTH-1 · MASTG-TEST-0355 · MASTG-BEST-0049

**Read more:** [book §17.4](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/07-platform-surfaces-and-new-frontiers.md#174-content-providers)

### AND-059: WebView runs JavaScript with content access on

**Severity:** medium · **Profiles:** MAS-L1 · **Confidence:** medium · **Effort:** minutes

**Why it matters:** `allowContentAccess` is on by default on every Android version. A page script in a WebView with JavaScript on can then read `content://` URIs the app can open, including its own providers. A WebView that loads only web pages is reported as low, since a web page can't open `content://` URLs.

**Fix:** Set `settings.allowContentAccess = false`, and load local content through `WebViewAssetLoader` over https.

**Verify:** Load a test page that fetches a `content://` URI of your app and confirm the request fails.

**IDs:** MASWE-0034 · MASVS-PLATFORM-2 · MASTG-TEST-0250 · MASTG-BEST-0013

**Read more:** [book §16.3](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/07-platform-surfaces-and-new-frontiers.md#163-file-access-the-setting-nobody-remembers-changing)

### AND-060: App writes to shared external storage

**Severity:** medium · **Profiles:** MAS-L1 · **Confidence:** medium · **Effort:** hours

**Why it matters:** Files in shared storage (Downloads, Documents, the external storage root) are outside the app sandbox. Other apps with storage access can read them, and they stay after the app is uninstalled. A write with no sign of sensitive data, such as a download the user asked for, is reported as low.

**Fix:** Keep sensitive files in `filesDir`, and let the user choose where exports go with the Storage Access Framework.

**Verify:** Run the export and download flows and confirm no file with personal data appears under `/sdcard`.

**IDs:** MASWE-0002 · MASVS-STORAGE-1 · MASTG-TEST-0202

**Read more:** [book Chapter 0.4](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/00-foundations.md#chapter-04-what-the-platforms-give-you-for-free)

### AND-061: File is readable or writable by every app

**Severity:** high · **Profiles:** MAS-L1 · **Confidence:** high · **Effort:** minutes

**Why it matters:** `MODE_WORLD_READABLE` and `setReadable(true, false)` open a file in the app's private folder to every app on the device, which defeats the sandbox for that file.

**Fix:** Use `MODE_PRIVATE`, and share files with other apps through FileProvider.

**Verify:** Run `adb shell run-as <package> ls -l files shared_prefs` and confirm no file is readable by others.

**IDs:** MASWE-0002 · MASVS-STORAGE-1

**Read more:** [book Chapter 0.4](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/00-foundations.md#chapter-04-what-the-platforms-give-you-for-free)

### AND-062: StrictMode logging ships in release

**Severity:** low · **Profiles:** MAS-R · **Confidence:** high · **Effort:** minutes

**Why it matters:** StrictMode reports disk, network and leak details with stack traces to logcat. Left on in release, it tells anyone reading the log which files and endpoints the app touches.

**Fix:** Set StrictMode policies only under `if (BuildConfig.DEBUG)`.

**Verify:** Install the release build and confirm `adb logcat -s StrictMode` stays empty while you use the app.

**IDs:** MASWE-0061 · MASVS-RESILIENCE-3 · MASTG-TEST-0265

**Read more:** [book §14.1](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/05-resilience.md#141-the-cheap-things-which-you-should-simply-do)

### AND-063: Release build keeps native debug symbols

**Severity:** low · **Profiles:** MAS-R · **Confidence:** high · **Effort:** minutes

**Why it matters:** Unstripped native libraries carry function names and debug information, which makes them much easier to read and patch. Play can symbolize native crashes from a separate symbols file instead.

**Fix:** Remove `keepDebugSymbols` and `doNotStrip`, and set `ndk { debugSymbolLevel = "FULL" }` to upload symbols separately.

**Verify:** Run `llvm-nm -D` on a `.so` from the release APK and confirm only exported symbols remain.

**IDs:** MASWE-0061 · MASVS-RESILIENCE-3 · MASTG-TEST-0288

**Read more:** [book §14.1](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/05-resilience.md#141-the-cheap-things-which-you-should-simply-do)

### AND-064: APK is signed with the v1 (JAR) scheme only

**Severity:** medium · **Profiles:** MAS-L1 · **Confidence:** high · **Effort:** minutes

**Why it matters:** The v1 scheme signs individual files, so on devices without the December 2017 patch the Janus bug lets an attacker change the app's code without breaking the signature. The v2 and v3 schemes sign the whole APK.

**Fix:** Remove `enableV2Signing = false`. AGP signs with v2 and v3 by default.

**Verify:** Run `apksigner verify --verbose app-release.apk` and confirm v2 or v3 shows `true`.

**IDs:** MASWE-0056 · MASVS-RESILIENCE-2 · MASTG-TEST-0224 · MASTG-BEST-0006

**Read more:** [book §14.1](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/05-resilience.md#141-the-cheap-things-which-you-should-simply-do)

### AND-065: Serializable object read from an Intent

**Severity:** medium · **Profiles:** MAS-L1 · **Confidence:** medium · **Effort:** hours

**Why it matters:** `getSerializableExtra` deserializes whatever class the sender chose. In a component other apps can start, a crafted object can run gadget code or crash the app.

**Fix:** Pass Parcelable or primitive extras, and on API 33+ read them with typed getters such as `getParcelableExtra(name, X::class.java)`.

**Verify:** Send the component an Intent with an unexpected Serializable class in that extra and confirm it's rejected.

**IDs:** MASWE-0050 · MASVS-CODE-4 · MASTG-TEST-0337

**Read more:** [book §19.4](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/07-platform-surfaces-and-new-frontiers.md#194-deserialization)

### AND-072: App requests fraud-relevant permissions

**Severity:** medium · **Profiles:** MAS-L2 · **Confidence:** medium · **Effort:** hours

**Why it matters:** SMS, call log, overlay, package visibility, install and accessibility access are what banking malware abuses to read one-time codes and take over the screen. Play restricts them, and each one needs a written reason.

**Fix:** Remove the permission, or move the feature to a narrower API (SMS Retriever, the photo picker, package queries). Keep a written justification for any that remain.

**Verify:** Check the merged release manifest and confirm each listed permission maps to a feature with a Play declaration.

**IDs:** MASWE-0066 · MASVS-PRIVACY-1 · MASTG-TEST-0254

**Read more:** [book §18.1](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/07-platform-surfaces-and-new-frontiers.md#181-permissions-ask-for-less-later-and-explain-why)

### AND-073: SSLSocket doesn't check the server's host name

**Severity:** high · **Profiles:** MAS-L1 · **Confidence:** medium · **Effort:** hours

**Why it matters:** An SSLSocket checks that the certificate is valid, but not that it belongs to the host you connected to. An attacker with a valid certificate for any other site can then read and change the traffic.

**Fix:** After the handshake, check the session with `HttpsURLConnection.getDefaultHostnameVerifier().verify(host, socket.session)` and close the socket if it fails. Or set `endpointIdentificationAlgorithm = "HTTPS"` on the socket's `SSLParameters`. Better still, use HttpsURLConnection or OkHttp, which do this check for you.

**Verify:** Connect the app to a server that presents a valid certificate for a different host name (for example wrong.host.badssl.com) and confirm the connection fails.

**IDs:** MASWE-0027 · MASVS-NETWORK-1 · MASTG-TEST-0234 · MASTG-DEMO-0048

**Read more:** [book §7.1](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/03-data-in-transit.md#71-the-baseline)

### AND-074: Keystore key stays unlocked long after authentication

**Severity:** medium · **Profiles:** MAS-L2 · **Confidence:** high · **Effort:** hours

**Why it matters:** A key with a long validity window can be used for that whole time after one fingerprint or PIN check. Someone who picks up the unlocked phone, or malware on it, can use the key without the user.

**Fix:** Use `setUserAuthenticationParameters(0, KeyProperties.AUTH_BIOMETRIC_STRONG)` so every use of the key needs a new authentication, and pass a `CryptoObject` to the prompt. If you need a window, keep it to a few seconds.

**Verify:** Authenticate once, wait longer than the window you chose, then try the protected action and confirm the app asks for the biometric again.

**IDs:** MASWE-0020 · MASVS-AUTH-2 · MASTG-TEST-0330 · MASTG-DEMO-0093

**Read more:** [book §11.3](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/04-proving-who-is-calling.md#113-the-enrollment-problem-nobody-thinks-about)

### AND-075: WebView opens any URL with no allowlist

**Severity:** medium · **Profiles:** MAS-L1 · **Confidence:** medium · **Effort:** hours

**Why it matters:** The WebView follows every link and redirect without checking where it goes. A link or a hijacked redirect can load an attacker's page into a WebView that runs JavaScript inside your app.

**Fix:** In `shouldOverrideUrlLoading`, parse the URL and allow only https and the hosts you own. Open anything else in the browser, or block it. Run the same check before your own `loadUrl` calls.

**Verify:** Tap a link in the WebView that points to a host outside your allowlist and confirm it opens in the browser or is blocked.

**IDs:** MASWE-0035 · MASVS-PLATFORM-2 · MASTG-TEST-0398 · MASTG-DEMO-0157

**Read more:** [book §16.4](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/07-platform-surfaces-and-new-frontiers.md#164-loading-untrusted-content)

### AND-076: Sensitive field lets the keyboard learn what is typed

**Severity:** medium · **Profiles:** MAS-L2 · **Confidence:** medium · **Effort:** minutes

**Why it matters:** Keyboards learn the words typed into normal text fields and suggest them later. A password, one-time code, or card number typed there can show up as a suggestion, and keyboard apps can keep it.

**Fix:** Give secrets a password input type (`textPassword`, `numberPassword`). For other sensitive fields, add `textNoSuggestions` (`TYPE_TEXT_FLAG_NO_SUGGESTIONS`) and `imeOptions="flagNoPersonalizedLearning"`.

**Verify:** Type a test value into the field, then start typing it again in another app and confirm the keyboard doesn't suggest it.

**IDs:** MASWE-0036 · MASVS-PLATFORM-3 · MASTG-TEST-0258 · MASTG-DEMO-0064

**Read more:** [book §6.5](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/02-data-at-rest.md#65-the-leaks-that-are-not-about-encryption)

## iOS

### IOS-001: App Transport Security is turned off

**Severity:** high · **Profiles:** MAS-L1 · **Confidence:** high · **Effort:** minutes

**Why it matters:** NSAllowsArbitraryLoads turns ATS off for the whole app; NSAllowsArbitraryLoadsInWebContent turns it off for everything web views load. Anyone on the same network, such as public Wi-Fi, can then read and change plain HTTP traffic, including tokens and personal data.

**Fix:** Remove NSAllowsArbitraryLoads and NSAllowsArbitraryLoadsInWebContent from Info.plist (and any INFOPLIST_KEY_ build setting that adds them). If one host really needs HTTP, add a narrow NSExceptionDomains entry for that host only.

**Verify:** Build the release configuration, open an http:// URL your app uses, and confirm the request fails with an App Transport Security error.

**IDs:** MASWE-0026 · MASVS-NETWORK-1 · MASTG-TEST-0322

**Read more:** [book §7.1](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/03-data-in-transit.md#71-the-baseline)

### IOS-002: An ATS exception allows plain HTTP to a host

**Severity:** medium · **Profiles:** MAS-L1 · **Confidence:** high · **Effort:** hours

**Why it matters:** NSExceptionAllowsInsecureHTTPLoads lets the app talk to that host over plain HTTP. Anyone on the network path can read or change those requests and responses.

**Fix:** Move the host to HTTPS and delete the exception. If you can't yet, keep the exception to that one host, without NSIncludesSubdomains, and plan its removal.

**Verify:** Remove the exception, build the release configuration, and confirm every request to that host still works over https://.

**IDs:** MASWE-0026 · MASVS-NETWORK-1 · MASTG-TEST-0322

**Read more:** [book §7.1](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/03-data-in-transit.md#71-the-baseline)

### IOS-003: A TLS version below 1.2 is allowed

**Severity:** medium · **Profiles:** MAS-L1 · **Confidence:** high · **Effort:** minutes

**Why it matters:** ATS requires at least TLS 1.2. An NSExceptionMinimumTLSVersion of TLSv1.0 or TLSv1.1, or a URLSession minimum set that low, lets a connection fall back to old protocol versions with known weaknesses.

**Fix:** Delete the NSExceptionMinimumTLSVersion entry (ATS then enforces TLS 1.2), and set tlsMinimumSupportedProtocolVersion to .TLSv12 or higher in code.

**Verify:** Point a test build at a server limited to TLS 1.1 (for example `openssl s_server -accept 8443 -tls1_1 -cipher 'DEFAULT:@SECLEVEL=0' -cert cert.pem -key key.pem` behind a test hostname) and confirm the app refuses the connection.

**IDs:** MASWE-0026 · MASVS-NETWORK-1 · MASTG-TEST-0342 · MASTG-TEST-0343

**Read more:** [book §7.1](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/03-data-in-transit.md#71-the-baseline)

### IOS-004: A server-trust handler accepts certificates without validating them

**Severity:** critical · **Profiles:** MAS-L1 · **Confidence:** medium · **Effort:** hours

**Why it matters:** The authentication-challenge handler returns .useCredential for the server's trust without calling SecTrustEvaluateWithError. An attacker on the network can present any certificate, even a self-signed one, and read or change all traffic.

**Fix:** Validate the chain with SecTrustEvaluateWithError before anything else, cancel the challenge when it fails, and only then compare pins. If you don't pin, return .performDefaultHandling.

**Verify:** Route the app through a proxy whose CA the device does not trust (mitmproxy, §22.3) and confirm every request fails with a TLS error.

**IDs:** MASWE-0027 · MASVS-NETWORK-1 · MASTG-TEST-0396 · MASTG-TEST-0397

**Read more:** [book §8.10](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/03-data-in-transit.md#810-how-to-implement-it)

### IOS-005: Pinning code falls back to default handling when no pin matches

**Severity:** high · **Profiles:** MAS-L2 · **Confidence:** medium · **Effort:** minutes

**Why it matters:** The delegate compares pins but never cancels the challenge. When no pin matches it returns .performDefaultHandling, which accepts any publicly trusted certificate, so the pinning check never blocks anything.

**Fix:** Return .cancelAuthenticationChallenge when the chain fails validation and when no pin matches. Use .performDefaultHandling only for challenges that aren't server trust.

**Verify:** Make the pin set wrong in a test build and confirm requests fail with NSURLErrorCancelled (-999), as in §8.10.

**IDs:** MASWE-0028 · MASVS-NETWORK-2 · MASTG-TEST-0396

**Read more:** [book §8.10](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/03-data-in-transit.md#810-how-to-implement-it)

### IOS-006: Pinned domain has no backup pin

**Severity:** medium · **Profiles:** MAS-L2 · **Confidence:** high · **Effort:** hours

**Why it matters:** NSPinnedDomains pins never expire. With a single pin, a key rotation or a CA change locks every user on that build out of your servers until they install an update.

**Fix:** Add a second SPKI-SHA256-BASE64 entry: a backup key at a second CA, or a key you hold offline. If you list both CA and leaf identities, each list needs its own backup. With react-native-ssl-public-key-pinning, list two or more `publicKeyHashes` for each host.

**Verify:** Serve a test endpoint with a certificate issued for the backup key (or from the backup CA) and confirm the app connects. Then confirm that a certificate matching neither pin fails.

**IDs:** MASWE-0028 · MASVS-NETWORK-2

**Read more:** [book §8.6](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/03-data-in-transit.md#86-where-the-pins-live-static-dynamic-and-hybrid)

### IOS-007: No certificate pinning (needed for high-risk apps)

**Severity:** medium · **Profiles:** MAS-L2 · **Confidence:** medium · **Effort:** days · **Only for:** banking, identity, health, ecommerce-cards · **Reported in:** Hardening checklist

**Why it matters:** Without pinning, any certificate from a CA the device trusts is accepted, including a root installed through a configuration profile or MDM. For money and health data, the book recommends SPKI pinning on an intermediate with a backup.

**Fix:** Pin the SPKI of your intermediate CA with NSPinnedDomains (simplest) or a URLSessionDelegate that validates first, plus a backup pin and a written rotation runbook. Pin only if you can also run failure alerts, CT monitoring, and a protected kill switch (§8.7); if not, don't pin and rely on strict TLS plus CT (§8.9). In React Native, call `initializeSslPinning` (react-native-ssl-public-key-pinning) before the first request.

**Verify:** Make the device trust a proxy CA, then confirm requests to pinned hosts fail while an unpinned host still loads through the proxy (§8.10, step 1).

**Other apps:** Book §8.8: outside banking, health, identity, and apps that handle card numbers, strict TLS plus Certificate Transparency monitoring is a reasonable position, and pinning adds operational risk. Enterprise apps: trust your private CA explicitly instead (§8.8).

**IDs:** MASWE-0028 · MASVS-NETWORK-2 · MASTG-TEST-0385

**Read more:** [book §8.8](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/03-data-in-transit.md#88-the-decision-by-application-type)

### IOS-008: Keychain item is readable before the first unlock

**Severity:** high · **Profiles:** MAS-L2 · **Confidence:** high · **Effort:** minutes

**Why it matters:** kSecAttrAccessibleAlways (and AlwaysThisDeviceOnly) makes the item readable even before the user first unlocks the phone. These are the items forensic tools recover from a locked device. Apple deprecated the class in iOS 12.

**Fix:** Use kSecAttrAccessibleWhenUnlockedThisDeviceOnly. If background work needs the item while the phone is locked, use kSecAttrAccessibleAfterFirstUnlockThisDeviceOnly. In React Native, use ACCESSIBLE.WHEN_UNLOCKED_THIS_DEVICE_ONLY (react-native-keychain) or SecureStore.WHEN_UNLOCKED_THIS_DEVICE_ONLY (expo-secure-store).

**Verify:** Search the code for kSecAttrAccessibleAlways and confirm no match. On a test device, lock it and confirm background code that needs the item behaves as you expect.

**Read more:** [book §4.4](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/02-data-at-rest.md#44-data-protection-classes-the-decision-you-keep-getting-wrong)

### IOS-009: Keychain item can migrate to another device

**Severity:** low · **Profiles:** MAS-L2 · **Confidence:** medium · **Effort:** minutes

**Why it matters:** Without ThisDeviceOnly, the item can be restored from a backup onto another device. A session token then travels with the backup instead of staying on the phone it was issued to. KeychainAccess defaults to .afterFirstUnlock, which has the same problem.

**Fix:** Append ThisDeviceOnly: kSecAttrAccessibleWhenUnlockedThisDeviceOnly, or AfterFirstUnlockThisDeviceOnly for items that background work needs. With KeychainAccess, call .accessibility(.whenUnlockedThisDeviceOnly). Skip this for items you sync on purpose with kSecAttrSynchronizable. In React Native, pass `accessible: ACCESSIBLE.WHEN_UNLOCKED_THIS_DEVICE_ONLY` to react-native-keychain (its default is AFTER_FIRST_UNLOCK) and `keychainAccessible: SecureStore.WHEN_UNLOCKED_THIS_DEVICE_ONLY` to expo-secure-store (its default is WHEN_UNLOCKED).

**Verify:** Back up a test device, restore it onto a second device, and confirm the app asks the user to sign in again.

**IDs:** MASWE-0006 · MASVS-STORAGE-2

**Read more:** [book §4.4](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/02-data-at-rest.md#44-data-protection-classes-the-decision-you-keep-getting-wrong)

### IOS-010: File written with no Data Protection

**Severity:** medium · **Profiles:** MAS-L2 · **Confidence:** high · **Effort:** minutes

**Why it matters:** NSFileProtectionNone (.noFileProtection) leaves the file readable at all times, even before the first unlock after a restart. Anyone who extracts data from the device can read it.

**Fix:** Write sensitive files with .completeFileProtection, and exclude them from backup. Use completeUntilFirstUserAuthentication only for files background work must read while locked. Never set the com.apple.developer.default-data-protection entitlement to NSFileProtectionNone.

**Verify:** On a physical device, write the file, lock the phone, and confirm code that runs while locked can't read it (the simulator doesn't enforce Data Protection).

**IDs:** MASTG-TEST-0299

**Read more:** [book §4.4](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/02-data-at-rest.md#44-data-protection-classes-the-decision-you-keep-getting-wrong)

### IOS-011: Token or password stored in UserDefaults

**Severity:** medium · **Profiles:** MAS-L2 · **Confidence:** manual · **Effort:** hours

**Why it matters:** UserDefaults is a plain plist in the app container (or in the shared App Group container for UserDefaults(suiteName:)). It is copied into backups and is readable by anyone with access to the device's files. A long-lived token there can be lifted and replayed.

**Fix:** Keep short-lived tokens in memory. Store long-lived tokens and credentials in the Keychain with kSecAttrAccessibleWhenUnlockedThisDeviceOnly. Leave only non-secret settings in UserDefaults.

**Verify:** On the simulator, sign in, then run `grep -rl "eyJ" "$(xcrun simctl get_app_container booted <bundle id> data)/Library/Preferences"` and confirm there is no output. UserDefaults is a binary plist, so don't add `-I`. If your tokens aren't JWTs, search for a known part of one instead.

**IDs:** MASWE-0001 · MASVS-STORAGE-1 · MASTG-TEST-0300 · MASTG-TEST-0302 · MASTG-TEST-0388

**Read more:** [book §6.4](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/02-data-at-rest.md#64-the-uncomfortable-question-nobody-asked)

### IOS-012: Biometric check only flips a boolean

**Severity:** high · **Profiles:** MAS-L2 · **Confidence:** manual · **Effort:** days

**Why it matters:** LAContext.evaluatePolicy returns a success flag. An attacker with Frida calls your success branch without any Face ID or Touch ID happening, and the bypass takes minutes. Nothing cryptographic depends on the result.

**Fix:** Bind the prompt to a key: create a Secure Enclave key with SecAccessControl [.privateKeyUsage, .biometryCurrentSet] and sign a server challenge with it. The server accepts the action only with a valid signature.

**Verify:** Hook evaluatePolicy to report success (for example, `ios ui biometrics_bypass` in objection) and confirm the protected action still fails because no valid signature reaches the server.

**IDs:** MASWE-0020 · MASVS-AUTH-2 · MASTG-TEST-0266

**Read more:** [book §11.1](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/04-proving-who-is-calling.md#111-decorative-versus-real)

### IOS-013: Biometric key stays valid after a new fingerprint or face is enrolled

**Severity:** high · **Profiles:** MAS-L2 · **Confidence:** high · **Effort:** hours

**Why it matters:** With .biometryAny, someone who knows the device passcode can enroll their own fingerprint or face and then unlock your app's protected key. .biometryCurrentSet invalidates the key when the enrolled set changes.

**Fix:** Replace .biometryAny with .biometryCurrentSet, and handle the signing failure that follows an enrollment change by sending the user to re-enroll or to server-side step-up.

**Verify:** Add a new fingerprint or re-enroll Face ID on a test device, use the feature again, and confirm signing fails and the app asks the user to re-enroll.

**IDs:** MASWE-0022 · MASVS-AUTH-2 · MASTG-TEST-0270 · MASTG-TEST-0271

**Read more:** [book §11.3](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/04-proving-who-is-calling.md#113-the-enrollment-problem-nobody-thinks-about)

### IOS-014: Web view inspection is on in release builds

**Severity:** high · **Profiles:** MAS-L1 · **Confidence:** high · **Effort:** minutes

**Why it matters:** isInspectable = true lets anyone with the device and a Mac attach Safari's Web Inspector, read the page, and call your JavaScript bridge from a console.

**Fix:** Wrap the line in #if DEBUG so it never compiles into release builds. In React Native, pass `webviewDebuggingEnabled={__DEV__}`.

**Verify:** Install the release build on a device connected to a Mac, open a web view screen, and confirm your app doesn't appear in Safari's Develop menu.

**IDs:** MASWE-0063 · MASVS-RESILIENCE-4

**Read more:** [book §16.6](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/07-platform-surfaces-and-new-frontiers.md#166-cleanup-and-hygiene)

### IOS-015: Script message handler doesn't check who sent the message

**Severity:** high · **Profiles:** MAS-L1 · **Confidence:** manual · **Effort:** hours

**Why it matters:** WebKit has no origin allowlist for message handlers. Without a check on message.frameInfo, any page or iframe the web view loads, including an ad or an attacker's page, can call your native code.

**Fix:** In the handler, reject messages unless frameInfo.isMainFrame is true and frameInfo.securityOrigin is your https host. Then validate every argument, and let the server authorize the action.

**Verify:** Load a page from a different origin in the same web view, post a message to each handler name, and confirm every handler rejects it.

**IDs:** MASWE-0033 · MASVS-PLATFORM-2 · MASTG-TEST-0376 · MASTG-TEST-0377

**Read more:** [book §16.2](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/07-platform-surfaces-and-new-frontiers.md#162-the-javascript-bridge-and-why-its-the-sharpest-edge)

### IOS-016: UIWebView is still in the app

**Severity:** medium · **Profiles:** MAS-L1 · **Confidence:** high · **Effort:** hours

**Why it matters:** Apple deprecated UIWebView in iOS 12 and the App Store rejects apps and updates that use it. It also runs web content inside your app's process, unlike WKWebView.

**Fix:** Replace UIWebView with WKWebView. If the reference comes from a third-party SDK, update or remove that SDK.

**Verify:** Run `grep -r UIWebView` on the source and `nm -u` on the release binary, and confirm neither finds it.

**IDs:** MASWE-0035 · MASVS-PLATFORM-2 · MASTG-TEST-0331
